  "content": "# Literature benchmarks for the in-house 3D heliospheric MHD solver

Compiled 2026-10-17 by a literature-research subagent. All numbers carry a source (paper, figure/table/section, URL or DOI). Tags used throughout:

- **[text]**: number read verbatim in the source text or a table.
- **[fig]**: number read off a rendered figure by me (typical reading error ±5–10%).
- **[derived]**: my own arithmetic from source inputs (not a published number).
- **[UNVERIFIED]**: secondary source only, abstract only, or could not be checked in the primary text.

Units: speeds km/s, densities cm⁻³ (proton number density unless stated), B in nT, T in K.

---

## 1. Idealized published simulations that can be replicated exactly

### Summary of candidates

| Candidate | Exact inputs available? | Quantitative outputs available? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pizzo (1982) MHD equatorial-patch CIR, as re-run by Wiengarten et al. (2014, CRONOS) | Yes, full spec in Wiengarten §3 (open access) | Yes, 1 AU equatorial profiles of v, flow angles, n, T, \|B\|, p_T overlaid for both codes (Wiengarten Fig. 4b); shock evolution 2–9 AU (Fig. 5) | **Recipe A (best code-to-code benchmark)** |
| Hofmeister et al. (2026) EUHFORIA idealized circular HSS at 0.1 AU | Yes (§2), uniform fast/slow states with a step, 0.1–1.5 AU | Yes, 1 AU peak v, n_min, n_SIR, T_SIR, B_SIR, travel time vs stream diameter (Fig. 10); radial power laws (§4.1) | **Recipe B (closest to your 0.1 AU, EUHFORIA-like setup)**; arXiv preprint, not refereed |
| Pizzo (1978) 3D hydrodynamic single stream at 0.16 AU | Yes (NASA TM-79580, Table I and Figs. 3–4) | Yes, 1 AU equatorial v, n, u_φ for 3D/2D/1D (Fig. 11); 1D shock pair at 1.25 AU | **Recipe C (1D vs 3D, no B; tests shock-formation timing)** |
| Pizzo (1991) local tilted-dipole fronts; Pizzo (1994a,b) and Pizzo & Gosling (1994) global tilted dipole | No (paywalled; abstracts only) | Qualitative only from abstracts; Pizzo & Gosling (1994) results are at 5 AU (outside your 2.5 AU domain) | Not reproducible from accessible sources |
| Odstrcil & Pizzo (1999a,b,c) CME in tilted-dipole wind | Inner boundary 0.14 AU, outer 5.04 AU (part 1) or 1.04 AU (MHD paper), from abstracts; slow/fast states not accessible | No | Not reproducible from accessible sources |
| HUXt vs HelioMAS (Owens et al. 2020) | Kinematic, 30–236 R_s, 128 longitudes | Speed MAE vs MHD; residual-acceleration law | Use as a sanity check of residual acceleration, not as a full MHD benchmark |
| EUHFORIA default WSA boundary (Pomoell & Poedts 2018) | Yes (constants verified via two later EUHFORIA papers) | Model-vs-data statistics only (Section 3) | Use as the boundary prescription for realistic runs |

---

### Recipe A — Pizzo (1982) / Wiengarten et al. (2014) equatorial-patch CIR (MHD, γ = 1.5)

Sources:
- Wiengarten, T., Kleimann, J., Fichtner, H., Kühl, P., Kopp, A., Heber, B., Kissmann, R. (2014), ApJ 788, 80, doi:10.1088/0004-637X/788/1/80, arXiv:1406.0293, §2–3, Eq. 8, Figs. 3–5. https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.0293
- Pizzo, V. J. (1982), JGR 87(A6), 4374–4394, doi:10.1029/JA087iA06p04374 (original steady-state MHD solution; I did not read it — paywalled; its Fig. 5 is the boundary and Fig. 6 the 1 AU result, digitized by Wiengarten).

Setup **[text]** (Wiengarten §2–3):
- Ideal MHD with gravity, γ = 1.5, run in the corotating frame with Ω = 14.71°/day (Snodgrass & Ulrich 1990). Your inertial-frame code with a rotating boundary map is equivalent.
- Domain: r ∈ [0.3, 10] AU, linear Δr = 1 R_s; ϑ ∈ [0.1π, 0.9π]; φ ∈ [0, 2π/6] with periodic azimuthal boundaries (six identical streams per 360°). Δϑ = Δφ = 0.25°. Run to steady state.
- Inner boundary r₀ = 0.3 AU (super-magnetosonic everywhere):
  - v_r = v₀(1 + a), v₀ = 300 km/s, a ∈ [0, 1] → 300 km/s ambient slow, 600 km/s fast.
  - a = Σ_{m=1..M} 0.5[tanh(A(ξ_m + Δξ)) − tanh(A(ξ_m − Δξ)) − tanh(Aξ_m)], ξ_m = √((ϑ−ϑ₀)² + (φ−φ₀,m)²), with A = 30, Δξ = 13°, ϑ₀ = π/2, φ₀,m = (2m−1)π/M, M = 6 (Eq. 8; fitted by digitizing Pizzo's Fig. 5).
  - n = n₀(1 + a)^−1.5, n₀ = 120 cm⁻³; thermal pressure constant, T₀ = 0.16 MK in the ambient slow wind (so T ∝ 1/n; fast-wind n = 42.4 cm⁻³, T = 0.45 MK).
  - Pizzo used constant |B| = 45 nT. Wiengarten prescribed constant B_r,0 and B_φ,0 = −B_r,0 v_φ,0/v_r,0 (Parker spiral in the corotating frame), so |B| deviates slightly from 45 nT.
  - Inertial-frame azimuthal velocity u_φ,0 = Ω(R_c/r₀)·sinϑ with R_c = 1.5 R_s (Weber–Davis corotation radius), i.e., essentially zero.

Caveats on Eq. 8 (please read before implementing):
- **As printed, Eq. 8 is not self-consistent [derived].** The third term −tanh(Aξ_m) makes a → −0.5 far from the stream (v → 150 km/s), contradicting "a ∈ [0, 1]" and Fig. 4a (ambient 300 km/s). I verified that the printed equation in the PDF does contain this term. Use the two-tanh top hat a = 0.5[tanh(A(ξ+Δξ)) − tanh(A(ξ−Δξ))] (A in rad⁻¹), which gives a ∈ [0, 1].
- **The plotted boundary is wider than Δξ = 13° [fig].** In Wiengarten Fig. 4a (equatorial cut at 0.3 AU) the 50% points of the 300→600 km/s transition sit at φ ≈ 228° and ≈ 191.5° around the center at 210°. That is a half-width ≈ 18.5°, which equals √2 × 13° (the coincidence suggests a factor √2 in their ξ). The 10–90% transition width is ≈ 4–5°, consistent with A = 30 rad⁻¹. To reproduce the published 1 AU curves, match Fig. 4a: half-width ≈ 18.5° in the equatorial plane.
- **Pressure convention [derived].** The total pressure plotted in Fig. 4a (p_T ≈ 1400 pPa slow, ≈ 1300 pPa fast) is matched only if the thermal pressure is p = 2nkT. Check, slow wind: 2nkT = 530 pPa plus B²/2μ₀ = 842 pPa at 46 nT gives 1372 pPa. With p = nkT it would be 1107 pPa. Treat T as T_p = T_e.
- **Angle labels [derived].** The caption names the panels "flow angle in corotating frame φ and in inertial frame ψ", but the values imply the opposite. The panel labeled φ is ≈ 0.01° at 0.3 AU (= inertial u_φ/v_r from R_c = 1.5 R_s) and ±10° at 1 AU (east–west deflection). The panel labeled ψ is −24°/−12° at 0.3 AU and −50°/−36° at 1 AU, which equals −arctan(Ωr/v), i.e., the corotating-frame flow (field-line) angle.

Expected outputs at 1 AU, equatorial plane (Wiengarten Fig. 4b; black = CRONOS, red = Pizzo 1982):
- **[text]** Compression at the HSS leading edge at φ ≈ 187°. A forward wave (φ ≈ 196°) and a reverse wave (φ ≈ 177°) have already steepened into MHD shocks by 1 AU.
- **[fig]** Upstream slow wind at φ = 200°: v ≈ 335 km/s, n ≈ 4 cm⁻³, T ≈ 1×10⁴ K, |B| ≈ 2.5 nT.
- **[fig]** Peaks:
  - n_max ≈ 22.5 cm⁻³ (CRONOS) and ≈ 23.5 cm⁻³ (Pizzo) at φ ≈ 189°.
  - |B|_max ≈ 15 nT at ≈ 188°.
  - p_T,max ≈ 155 pPa at ≈ 187°.
  - T_max ≈ 2.0×10⁵ K at ≈ 188°.
- **[fig]** Speed profile: v rises 380 → 555 km/s at φ ≈ 189–187°, then 585 km/s at 178°. At the reverse shock (φ ≈ 177°) v jumps to ≈ 620 km/s while n drops 7 → 3 cm⁻³, T 155 → 85 kK and |B| 9 → 4.5 nT. The fast plateau is ≈ 600–615 km/s.
- **[fig]** Trailing rarefaction minimum near φ ≈ 153°: n ≈ 0.3–0.5 cm⁻³, |B| ≈ 0.7 nT.
- **[fig]** East–west flow deflection (the panel labeled φ): +10° (westward) just ahead of the interface, −7.5° behind it.
- **[fig]** Corotating-frame angle (the panel labeled ψ): −50° in slow wind, −36° in fast wind.
- **[text]** Beyond 1 AU (Fig. 5, 2–9 AU): forward and reverse shocks are more pronounced at 2 AU. The stream interface (SI) shifts 15° per panel. Shocks from adjacent CIRs (60° periodicity) meet just before 4 AU and form a CMIR; by 5 AU the CMIR compression exceeds the original SI compression.

Code-to-code agreement Wiengarten called "very satisfactory" **[text]**. Fig. 4b shows CRONOS–Pizzo differences of ≲ 5% in peak n and |B|, and ≲ 30 km/s in the rarefaction speed **[fig]**.

---

### Recipe B — Hofmeister et al. (2026) idealized EUHFORIA high-speed stream (0.1 → 1.5 AU)

Source: Hofmeister, S. J. et al. (2026), "MHD simulations on the large-scale propagation of high-speed solar wind streams," arXiv:2605.01613 (submitted 2026-05-02; **preprint, not refereed**). §2–6, Figs. 3, 4, 8, 10. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01613

Setup **[text]** (§2):
- EUHFORIA heliospheric MHD only (Pomoell & Poedts 2018), inner boundary sphere r = 0.1 AU.
- Circular patch of fast wind centered on the solar equator, embedded in uniform slow wind, step-function transition. Diameter varied 3°–36° (Fig. 10 extends to ≈ 47°).
- Fast: v_r = 650 km/s, n = 150 cm⁻³, gas pressure 3.3 nPa.
- Slow: v_r = 350 km/s, n = 500 cm⁻³, same 3.3 nPa.
- Uniform |B_r| = 325 nT (≈ 1.5 G at the surface; open flux 9×10¹⁴ Wb). The polarity inversion line is at latitude −30°·cos(longitude), included only for flux balance.
- Grid 0.1–1.5 AU, Δr = 0.0055 AU, 1.0° angular resolution. Relaxation 7 days, then quasi-steady corotating state.

Caveats:
- **γ is not stated [UNVERIFIED].** EUHFORIA's default is γ = 1.5. However, the paper normalizes T by (r/r₀)^{4/3}, the γ = 5/3 adiabatic scaling (Fig. 4 caption).
- **EUHFORIA heating matters.** The paper states (§4.1) that EUHFORIA applies "a small, artificial heating … to reproduce the residual solar wind acceleration up to 0.4 AU." An ideal-MHD solver without that heating should not reproduce the 650 → 730 km/s acceleration.

Expected outputs **[text]**:
- Uniform-flow states at 1 AU: HSS ≈ 730 km/s and 1.5 cm⁻³; slow wind ≈ 390 km/s and 5 cm⁻³.
- A boundary (shear) layer forms by 0.12 AU, of width ≈ 7°.
- HSS travel time 0.1 AU → 1 AU (front) is 2.8–3.6 days.
- 10° stream, stream center:
  - Peak v drops from 680 to 590 km/s between 1 and 4 days of travel.
  - Normalized SIR peak density (scaled by (r/r₀)², relative to the inner-boundary slow density) rises 1.07 → 1.86 (+74%).
  - Power-law fits n ∝ r^α give α = −1.48 (SIR peak), −1.63 (at peak v) and −1.91 (minimum density). A parcel from the stream core gives α = −1.44; a parcel from the trailing boundary layer gives −2.27.
- Fig. 8 case (stream diameter not stated in the text I read): SI speed 500 km/s at the stream center vs 430 km/s at the flank. Peak v is 700 vs 500 km/s.
- Between 0.2 and 1 AU, mass flux over the HSS interval rises ≈ 5%, and kinetic energy density falls ≈ 7%.

Expected outputs at 1 AU vs stream diameter (Fig. 10; virtual spacecraft at the stream's latitudinal center) **[fig]**:

| Diameter at 0.1 AU | v_peak | n_min | n_SIR,max | T_SIR,max | B_SIR,max | Δt (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3° | 425 | 3.7 | 4.9 | 85 kK | 5.1 nT | 3.6 |
| ≈ 11° | 648 | 1.5 | 7.7 | 290 kK | 8.4 nT | 3.1 |
| ≈ 20° | 710 | 0.95 | 9.0 | 300 kK | 10.3 nT | 3.0 |
| ≥ 30° (saturated) | 725–735 | 0.75–0.8 | 9.6–9.9 | ≈ 300 kK | 10.9–11.4 nT | 2.9–3.0 |

- **[text]** n_min saturates at ≈ 0.7 cm⁻³ for large streams, below the 1.5 cm⁻³ expected from pure spherical expansion. The global peak velocity saturates at 730 km/s for diameters ≳ 14°.
- **[text]** The authors note that "MHD simulations generally tend to underestimate plasma compression in stream interaction regions" (§2).

My consistency checks for these inputs **[derived]**:
- **Density convention.** EUHFORIA's default n_fsw = 300 cm⁻³ with ρ_fsw = 0.5 n_fsw m_p (see Recipe D) suggests EUHFORIA's "n" counts electrons + protons. Hofmeister's fast-wind 150 cm⁻³ equals 0.5 × 300 and reproduces 1.5 cm⁻³ at 1 AU, so I read Hofmeister's n as proton density. Then P = 3.3 nPa = 2 n_p k T gives T ≈ 0.80 MK (fast) and 0.24 MK (slow).
- **Super-critical boundary.** At 0.1 AU, v_A ≈ 580 km/s (fast) and ≈ 320 km/s (slow), so the slow wind is only marginally super-fast-magnetosonic (fast-mode speed ≈ 330 km/s vs v = 350 km/s). If you use these values, check that every boundary cell is super-critical.
- **Ideal (no-heating) Bernoulli terminal speeds at 1 AU, gravity included:**

  | Wind | γ = 5/3 | γ = 1.5 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Fast (650 at 0.1 AU) | ≈ 685 km/s | ≈ 690 km/s |
  | Slow (350 at 0.1 AU) | ≈ 354 km/s | ≈ 360 km/s |

  Without gravity, ≈ 697 (fast) and ≈ 376 (slow) for γ = 5/3. The 730/390 km/s quoted above therefore include ≈ 35–45 km/s from EUHFORIA's heating. The magnetic-rotational (Weber–Davis) energy term adds ≲ 2 km/s.

---

### Recipe C — Pizzo (1978) 3D hydrodynamic single stream at 0.16 AU (γ = 5/3, no B)

Source: Pizzo, V. (1978), "A three-dimensional model of corotating streams in the solar wind. 1. Theoretical foundations," NASA TM-79580 (preprint of JGR 83, 5563, 1978). Table I, Figs. 3, 4, 11 and text pp. 14–24. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19780020088/downloads/19780020088.pdf

Setup:
- **[text]** Steady corotating polytropic hydrodynamics with gravity, γ = 5/3 (chosen as adiabatic; this forces "elevated" coronal T and gives net radial acceleration).
- **[text]** Inner boundary r₀ = 35 R_s = 0.16 AU. Slow flow (Table I) at r₀: u = 290 km/s, n = 370 cm⁻³, T = 1.12×10⁶ K, u_θ = u_φ = 0.
- **[text]** Stream: u = 290 + 290·S(θ)S(φ), peak 580 km/s at the equator. The text gives the variations "in both θ and φ … of the form [sin(πx)/(πx)]², |x| ≤ 1." Only u varies; n, T, u_θ, u_φ stay at slow-flow values. The 1D (r, t) comparison is Hundhausen's (1973) model. Streams repeat every 120° (periodic in φ, non-interacting).
- **[fig]** The angular half-width at which x = 1 is not stated in the text. From the 300/390/480 km/s contours on the 10° grid of Fig. 3 I estimate x = (angle from center)/≈ 27°, i.e., zero-amplitude half-width ≈ 26–27° in both latitude and longitude. The contours are rounded squares, consistent with a separable product.

Expected outputs:
- **[text]** Table I, slow flow at 1.0 AU: u = 401 km/s, n = 7.1 cm⁻³, T = 8.0×10⁴ K.
- **[derived]** I checked Table I. Mass flux is conserved to 0.2%, and T ∝ n^{2/3} is exact. Bernoulli is conserved (8.28×10¹⁰ m²/s² at both radii) **only with P = 2nkT**. This is a clean 1D acceleration test: a uniform slow flow should go 290 → 401 km/s.
- **[fig]** 1 AU equatorial profile (Fig. 11, 3D nonlinear):
  - Peak u ≈ 625 km/s on a 400 km/s base.
  - Peak n ≈ 18 cm⁻³; 2D gives ≈ 20.5 and 1D ≈ 31, on a 7.1 base. Trailing rarefaction minimum ≈ 4.2 cm⁻³.
  - u_φ +28/−18 km/s (3D) across the interaction; 1D has u_φ ≡ 0.
- **[text]** Shock formation:
  - The 1D (r, t) model forms a shock pair "near 1.25 AU."
  - The 2D/3D models "do not shock before 1.5 AU," because nonradial flow relieves the compression.
  - A purely kinematic model "shocks near 0.8 AU."
- **[text]** Net latitudinal mass transport away from the equator reaches 4.5% at 1.5 AU. Nonradial effects matter mainly inside ≈ 0.75 AU.

This recipe isolates (i) radial acceleration under γ = 5/3 with gravity and (ii) the 1D-vs-3D delay of shock formation. Run with B = 0 (or B ≈ 10⁻³ of equipartition) to compare with the hydrodynamic result.

---

### Recipe D — EUHFORIA / ENLIL default empirical boundary (for realistic runs)

**EUHFORIA** (Pomoell & Poedts 2018, J. Space Weather Space Clim. 8, A35, doi:10.1051/swsc/2018020). I could not open the primary text (bot wall). The constants below are quoted identically in two later EUHFORIA-team papers whose text I read:
- Samara et al. (2021), A&A 648, A35, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202039325, arXiv:2102.06617, §2.1, Eqs. 1–5 and §5.
- Samara et al. (2024), arXiv:2405.09693, §2, Eqs. 1–5 and §5 (journal not verified).

The prescription **[text]**:
- f = (R_s/R_b)²·B_r(R_s)/B_b(R_b), R_b = 0.1 AU (Eq. 1).
- v_r(f, d) = 240 + 675/(1+f)^0.222 · [1 − 0.8 exp(−(d/0.02)^1.25)]³ km/s, where d is the angular distance in rad of the field-line footpoint to the nearest coronal-hole boundary (Samara 2021 Eq. 2).
- n = n_fsw (v_fsw/v_r)²; T = T_fsw (ρ_fsw/ρ); B_r = sgn(B_corona)·B_fsw·(v_r/v_fsw).
- v_fsw = 675 km/s, B_fsw = 300 nT at 0.1 AU, n_fsw = 300 cm⁻³, thermal pressure constant = 3.3 nPa (T_fsw = 0.8 MK), ρ_fsw = 0.5 n_fsw m_p.
- Meridional B is set to zero at 0.1 AU, so B_z is "severely underestimated" (Samara 2021 §5).

Ad hoc steps and grid **[text]**:
- From Samara 2024 §2: 50 km/s are subtracted from v at 0.1 AU, and speeds are capped to [275, 625] km/s (the lower cap avoids sub-Alfvénic cells).
- γ = 1.5 (Samara 2024 §5). There, changing γ to 1.1 or 5/3 changed 1 AU temperature noticeably but speed only mildly.
- Standard grid in Samara 2021 §5: 4° × 4° (90 × 30 cells) × 512 radial cells, Δr ≈ 0.0037 AU, 0.1–2 AU.

Density convention **[derived]**: ρ = 0.5 n m_p implies EUHFORIA's n counts all particles. Fast-wind proton density at 0.1 AU = 150 cm⁻³ (1.5 cm⁻³ at 1 AU before compression), and P = n_total·k·T.

**ENLIL** — no primary text read. Two secondary sources give its boundary settings.

MacNeice (2010) slides, "Preparing heliospheric models for space weather operation," NOAA Space Weather Workshop, slide "WSA/ENLIL (Odstrcil)" **[text, secondary]** (https://www.spaceweather.gov/sites/default/files/images/u33/MACNEICE%20SWW%202010.pdf):
- Rotating inner boundary at 21.5 R_s, outer boundary 2 AU.
- v → (v − 50) km/s, floor 250 and ceiling 650 km/s.
- n v² = 300 × 650² (constant kinetic-energy flux); n T = 300 × 0.8 (constant pressure; n in cm⁻³, T in MK).
- Azimuthal B added (Parker spiral), plus an azimuthal offset for the 1 → 21.5 R_s travel time.

Jian et al. (2016, Space Weather, doi:10.1002/2016SW001435), as relayed by my validation sub-search **[UNVERIFIED by me]**: an ENLIL v2.8 alternative setting raises the B scaling factor 2 → 4 and lowers the inner-boundary fast-wind density 200 → 125 cm⁻³.

Also: Wiengarten et al. (2014) §2 confirms γ = 1.5 "as used in the heliospheric part of the ENLIL setup (Odstrcil et al. 2004)" **[text]**.

---

### Other published reference points for model behavior

- **Residual acceleration beyond 30 R_s** (Owens et al. 2020, Sol. Phys. 295, 43, doi:10.1007/s11207-020-01605-3, §2 Eq. 4, https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/89616/):
  - **[text]** HelioMAS v_r(r) is matched by V(r) = V₀[1 + α(1 − exp(−(r − r₀)/r_H))] with α = 0.15, r_H = 50 R_s, r₀ = 30 R_s (from Riley & Lionello 2011, Sol. Phys. 270, 575).
  - **[derived]** At 1 AU this is +14.6% (e.g., 400 → 458 km/s).
- **HUXt vs HelioMAS** (Owens et al. 2020, §3–4) **[text]**:
  - Equatorial-plane speed MAE 15.7 km/s (≈ 4%) for CR1833; 25.6 km/s (6.4%) averaged over 578 CRs.
  - The MHD solution has a more gradual slow→fast transition than the upwind model.
  - A 1000 km/s CME-like pulse at 30 R_s takes ≈ 2.82 days to 1 AU. HelioMAS arrives 0.2 days (4.8 h) earlier than HUXt by the maximum-gradient criterion; peak-v times agree within 1 h.
- **Shock formation, classic 1D** (Hundhausen 1973, JGR 78, 1528, doi:10.1029/JA078i010p01528). **[UNVERIFIED: abstract only]** A coronal temperature disturbance at 28 R_s reproduces 1 AU stream profiles; streams steepen and form a shock pair "at slightly greater distances" than 1 AU.
- **Shock formation, observations and theory** (Richardson 2018, Living Rev. Sol. Phys. 15, 1, doi:10.1007/s41116-017-0011-z, §"Observations of SIRs beyond 1 AU", open access at PMC6390897) **[text]**:
  - "The Pioneer 10 and 11 observations demonstrated that such shocks tend to form beyond 2 AU," and "by 3–5 AU, over 90% of interaction regions were found to have forward shocks and ∼75% reverse shocks."
  - The same review (§"Observations of SIRs inside 1 AU") quotes Schwenn (1990): of ~25 Helios forward-shock candidates only ~6 were fully developed shocks. Richardson's crude estimate is that only ~2% (forward) to <4% (reverse) of interaction regions inside 1 AU have shocks. Corotating shock rate is ~1 per 200 days inside 0.5 AU vs ~1 per 100 days at 0.5–1 AU.
- **Gosling & Pizzo (1999)**, Space Sci. Rev. 89, 21–52, doi:10.1023/A:1005291711900. **Not accessible** (paywalled; I found no copy). As cited by Richardson (2018) §"Ulysses" **[text]**:
  - Forward waves propagate equatorward and reverse waves poleward in a tilted-dipole geometry.
  - Ulysses saw reverse shocks persist to higher latitudes than forward shocks.
  - Meridional deflections are equatorward behind forward shocks and poleward ahead of reverse shocks.
- **Pizzo (1991)**, JGR 96, 5405–5420, doi:10.1029/91JA00155 **[UNVERIFIED: abstract only, via EarthRef https://earthref.org/ERR/32225/]**:
  - At 0.3–0.6 AU, tilted-dipole stream interfaces show nonradial deflections of "only a few degrees," with N–S dominant.
  - The total deflection scales ≈ sin α (α = dipole tilt); the N–S/E–W ratio scales ≈ cot α.
  - Magnetic torques matter inside ≈ 0.5 AU.
- **Pizzo & Gosling (1994)**, GRL 21, 2063, doi:10.1029/94GL01581 **[UNVERIFIED: abstract only]**: at ~5 AU, forward shocks vanish poleward of the streamer-belt edge while reverse shocks persist.
- **Riley et al. (2012)**, JASTP 83, 11–21, doi:10.1016/j.jastp.2012.01.019, §4 (author copy https://www.predsci.com/~pete/research/eric-priest/riley12b.pdf) **[text]**:
  - At 1 AU in cycle 23, forward CIR shocks outnumber reverse ≈ 3:1 (ratio > 10 in 1997).
  - There were 3–4× more reverse shocks in the 2008 minimum than in 1996.
  - From Jian et al. (2011), 39% of CIRs had shocks in the recent minimum, more than double the previous minimum.
  - MAS modeling attributes the F/R asymmetry to CIR tilt: ecliptic spacecraft see the equatorward flanks, and F shocks penetrate to lower latitudes.

**Synthesis.**
- Speed: ambient-wind models reach speed RMSE ≈ 75–125 km/s (typically ≈ 100) and hourly r ≈ 0.3–0.6. That is no better than 27-day persistence (RMSE ≈ 80–120).
- Density: the worst-reproduced parameter (r ≲ 0.3). WSA-ENLIL has a roughly unbiased median but flattens SIR peaks (max ≈ ×0.5, min ≈ ×2). MAS-ENLIL, CORHEL and EUHFORIA 1.0.4 over-predict density up to ×2. At Mars, WSA-ENLIL under-predicts density (median ×0.49) and over-predicts speed (+70 km/s).
- B: under-predicted unless rescaled (×2 to ×5), a consequence of the open-flux deficit; ENLIL applies a scaling factor.
- High-speed events: POD 0.37–0.64, FAR 0.25–0.5, timing errors ≈ 1 day (0.5–2.1 d).
- Data assimilation: the largest verified gain, −18% to −31% in speed RMSE (Lang & Owens 2019; Lang et al. 2021).
